topics.topic: Whether the backup instant is recorded at transaction opening or snapshot fixation
questions: Is the recorded instant taken when the read transaction is begun, or when its first read fixes the SQLite snapshot?
Is the backup instant sampled when the read transaction is opened or when its first read fixes the SQLite snapshot?

quotes: a backup's instant is the one `store` reads when the copy's read transaction begins, which `backups` records and never reads itself.

The copy answers, from its one read transaction, the instant of the read that fixed its snapshot and the last sequence number the audit counter it holds says (A15 rule 5), so a backup's record describes exactly its copy (A18 rule 1).
judgement.divergence: The backup records either the transaction-opening instant or the later snapshot-fixing instant; the owner reading the backup record or newest-backup instant notices.
judgement.why: The two passages assign the recorded backup instant to different events.

bases.passage: a backup's instant is the one `store` reads when the copy's read transaction begins, which `backups` records and never reads itself.

The copy answers, from its one read transaction, the instant of the read that fixed its snapshot and the last sequence number the audit counter it holds says (A15 rule 5), so a backup's record describes exactly its copy (A18 rule 1).
bases.rests_on: The copy's read transaction fixes its snapshot by its first read, which is of the audit counter's last sequence number, and the instant is read from the clock at that read; a change committed after it is not in this backup, which holds the store as its snapshot saw it, and a later backup holds whatever the store holds when its own snapshot is fixed.

unsupported_sides: a backup's instant is the one `store` reads when the copy's read transaction begins, which `backups` records and never reads itself.

witness.initial: A backup read transaction has begun, but its first read has not yet fixed the snapshot.
events: A writing action commits after the backup read transaction begins.
`store` performs the first read of the audit counter and fixes a snapshot containing that action.
`backups` records the instant returned for the backup.
outcomes: The backup records the earlier instant when its read transaction began.
The backup records the later instant of the read that fixed its snapshot.
witness.observer: The owner reading the backup's record or newest-backup instant.
basis: A backup is a consistent copy of the store taken while Registry runs: one snapshot of the store, as one read transaction sees it, while other transactions go on; it never holds part of a transaction, and its recorded instant and last sequence number are those of that snapshot, the instant being that of the read that fixes its snapshot (below).

The copy's read transaction fixes its snapshot by its first read, which is of the audit counter's last sequence number, and the instant is read from the clock at that read; a change committed after it is not in this backup, which holds the store as its snapshot saw it, and a later backup holds whatever the store holds when its own snapshot is fixed.

topics.topic: Handling temporary database sidecar files after interrupted new-store creation
questions: After interruption while a new store is being built under its temporary name in write-ahead-log mode, what must the next start do with sidecar files belonging to that temporary database?

quotes: `capability:store.open_store` first removes a file of the store's temporary name — the store's name with the suffix the release declares — and no other file.

a new store is made in write-ahead-log mode (A18 rule 1); otherwise it opens the store for reading and writing, puts it in that mode when it is not — a store that cannot be put in it stops the start —, runs the full integrity check and compares the store version with the release's (A17 rule 5).
judgement.why: The texts do not state that creating the temporary store can leave sidecar files, what effects such files have, or that any capability must remove them, so the proposed witness cannot be built from the texts.

topics.topic: Required ordering and causality between the clock read and snapshot-fixing database read
questions: When a clock read cannot be atomic with SQLite's first snapshot-fixing read, which must occur first, and what causal relation must the recorded instant have to transactions included in the snapshot?

quotes: The copy's read transaction fixes its snapshot by its first read, which is of the audit counter's last sequence number, and the instant is read from the clock at that read; a change committed after it is not in this backup, which holds the store as its snapshot saw it, and a later backup holds whatever the store holds when its own snapshot is fixed.
judgement.why: The precise contractual meaning and causal relation of the recorded backup instant to the snapshot belongs to State 6 contracts, while State 4 already names `copy_store_snapshot` as the capability producing both values.

topics.topic: Whether write-ahead-log conversion is retained or rolled back after a later startup failure
questions: When start converts an existing store to write-ahead-log mode and a listener then fails, must the mode change remain, or must the store be restored to its former journal mode?
If an existing store is successfully changed to write-ahead-log mode but then fails integrity or version checking, is that journal-mode change retained or rolled back?

quotes: a new store is made in write-ahead-log mode (A18 rule 1); otherwise it opens the store for reading and writing, puts it in that mode when it is not — a store that cannot be put in it stops the start —, runs the full integrity check and compares the store version with the release's (A17 rule 5).
An existing store is left as it was.
judgement.divergence: After a later listener failure, the existing store either remains converted to write-ahead-log mode or retains its former journal mode; the owner or the next start notices.
judgement.why: The startup flow both changes an existing store's journal mode and says a later listener failure leaves that store as it was.

witness.initial: A valid existing store uses a journal mode other than write-ahead-log mode.
events: `store` opens the existing store and puts it in write-ahead-log mode.
`instance_lifecycle` cannot open a listener and stops the start.
outcomes: The existing store remains in write-ahead-log mode because the store-opening step changed it.
The existing store remains in its former journal mode because the listener-failure passage leaves it as it was.
witness.observer: The owner or the next Registry start inspecting the store's journal mode.
basis: The host starts the Registry process — first start, a restart, or a start after the owner put a store in place of a lost one (A18 rule 8).
